TC ID & Scenario: TC05 (Logic - Empty Target): Trigger weather campaign on a perfectly sunny day nationwide.

TC ID & Scenario: TC07 (Security - Idempotency): Trigger the birthday cron-job 3 times on the same day.
Expected Result: HTTP 200 on all calls. However, DB checks ensure users only receive EXACTLY ONE birthday voucher per year. No duplicates issued.

TC ID & Scenario: TC08 (Logic - Milestone): Trigger the milestone scanner.
Expected Result: HTTP 200, users who just reached their 10th wash in the DB are upgraded to Silver Tier and receive a milestone voucher.

TC ID & Scenario: TC09 (Happy Path): Super Admin evaluates Branch A's performance.

TC ID & Scenario: TC10 (Security - RBAC Hierarchy): A Manager from Branch A attempts to call this Super Admin endpoint for Branch B.
Expected Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden, "Access denied. Super Admin role required".

TC ID & Scenario: TC11 (Scale & Performance): Trigger the global revenue AI on all 50 branches simultaneously.
Expected Result: HTTP 202 Accepted. The API immediately returns an acknowledgment, pushing the heavy aggregation tasks to a background Queue (Kafka/Redis) to prevent HTTP timeouts.

TC ID & Scenario: TC12 (Logic - Isolation): Ensure Branch A's underperformance triggers vouchers ONLY for customers geographically linked to Branch A, not nationwide.
Expected Result: DB verification shows localized voucher distribution.

TC ID & Scenario: TC13 (Happy Path): Admin creates a Manager profile for Branch X.
Expected Result: HTTP 201, credentials generated, welcome email dispatched via SES/SendGrid.

TC ID & Scenario: TC14 (Logic - Limit Exceeded): Branch X already has 2 active Managers (Maximum allowed).
Expected Result: HTTP 400, "Maximum number of managers reached for this branch".

TC ID & Scenario: TC15 (Security - Token Revocation): Admin changes a Manager's status to `Terminated`.
Expected Result: HTTP 200. System MUST instantly revoke all active Access Tokens and Refresh Tokens belonging to that Manager. Any ongoing API calls by the Manager fail with HTTP 401.

TC ID & Scenario: TC16 (Security - Self Termination): A Super Admin attempts to terminate their own account.
Expected Result: HTTP 400, "Cannot terminate your own Super Admin account".

TC ID & Scenario: TC17 (Happy Path - Price Hike): Admin increases the price of "Standard Wash" from 100k to 120k.
Expected Result: HTTP 200, global catalog updated.

TC ID & Scenario: TC18 (Logic - Active Bookings Impact): Admin updates the price, but there are currently 50 `Pending` bookings made at the old price (100k).
Expected Result: The system strictly honors the old price (100k) for existing bookings (Price snapshotting). Only new bookings created after the timestamp use the 120k price.

TC ID & Scenario: TC19 (Logic - Deactivation): Admin deactivates a service that is currently included in 10 future bookings.
Expected Result: HTTP 409 Conflict, "Cannot deactivate service. There are active bookings depending on this service. Please resolve them first."

TC ID & Scenario: TC20 (Data Integrity - Soft Delete): Admin deletes a service.
Expected Result: HTTP 200. The service is `Soft Deleted` (`isActive = false`) rather than hard deleted to preserve historical wash logs and financial reports.

TC ID & Scenario: TC21 (Happy Path): The AI failed to categorize a rare vehicle model. Super Admin manually approves it as a "Luxury SUV".
Expected Result: HTTP 200, mapping is saved globally. Future AI detections for this exact make/model will automatically classify it as a Luxury SUV without manual intervention.

TC ID & Scenario: TC22 (Logic - Downgrade Impact): Admin corrects a vehicle mistakenly registered as an "SUV" down to a "Sedan". The customer has a `Pending` booking for an "SUV Premium Wash" (which is incompatible with Sedans).
Expected Result: HTTP 200. The system automatically flags the `Pending` booking as a `Mismatch` or sends an SMS to the customer advising them that their booked service has been adjusted.

TC ID & Scenario: TC23 (Budget Overflow): Create a Fixed Amount voucher (e.g., 500,000 VND discount) with a `MaxGlobalUsage` of 1,000,000. Ensure the internal Campaign Budget tracker does not suffer from 32-bit Integer Overflow (500 Billion VND).
TC24 (Logic - Time Paradox): Create a voucher where `StartDate` = `2026-12-31` and `EndDate` = `2026-01-01` (End date is before start date). System must strictly reject.
TC25 (Logic - Infinite Usage): Set `MaxGlobalUsage` to `-1` or `null` to indicate unlimited budget. Verify the DB handles infinity constraints correctly without hanging.
TC26 (Validation - SQL Injection): Inject nested SQL into the JSON array of `ApplicableBranchIds`: `[1, 2, "3) OR (1=1"]`.
TC27 (API Limit - External Gateway): Trigger the weather API, but the external provider (OpenWeather) is down or rate-limiting the server.
Expected Result: System gracefully falls back, logs `Third_Party_Timeout`, and does NOT crash the internal voucher distribution engine.

TC ID & Scenario: TC28 (Scale - 1 Million Users): Rain detected nationwide. System must distribute vouchers to 1,000,000 users.
Expected Result: API must return HTTP 202 Accepted instantly. Background workers (RabbitMQ/Kafka) must chunk the distribution (e.g., batches of 10,000) to prevent Out of Memory (OOM) crashes and DB transaction log full errors.

TC ID & Scenario: TC29 (State - Accidental Double Trigger): Super Admin runs the weather trigger, gets impatient (UI freezing), and clicks it 5 more times.
Expected Result: Strict Redis lock prevents duplicate campaigns from launching for the exact same weather event on the exact same day.

TC ID & Scenario: TC30 (Cascading Update - Price Change): Super Admin increases the price of "Premium Wash".

TC ID & Scenario: TC31 (Logic - Deactivation Lock): Super Admin attempts to deactivate the "Standard Wash" service (`isActive = false`), but it is currently mapped to active Phase 1 Booking endpoints.

TC ID & Scenario: TC32 (Financial Impact): AI previously categorized `51G-12345` as a Sedan. Customer paid 100k. Super Admin forces update to SUV.

TC ID & Scenario: TC33 (Consistency): Super Admin updates a Make/Model mapping (e.g., all "Honda CR-V"s are now "SUV").

TC ID & Scenario: TC34 (Timezone Shift): Run the analytics report for Jan 1st from a Server in UTC, while the Branch operates in UTC+7 (Vietnam).

TC ID & Scenario: TC35 (Math - Edge Precision): Summation of 10,000 micro-transactions. Verify DB `SUM()` function handles precise decimals (e.g., `DECIMAL(18,2)`) and avoids floating-point anomalies (e.g., returning `1000.000000001`).
TC36 (Logic - Excluded Revenue): Ensure `Cancelled` bookings with 100% refunds are strictly excluded from the "Gross Revenue" metrics.
TC37 (Logic - B2B Revenue): Ensure B2B Fleet washes (Postpaid) are accounted for in "Accrued Revenue" but distinctly separated from "Cash/Card Collected Revenue".

TC ID & Scenario: TC39 (Data Leak - Duplicate Email): Super Admin creates a Manager using an email that already belongs to a standard Customer.

TC ID & Scenario: TC40 (Security - JWT Blacklisting): Manager is terminated at 14:00:00. At 14:00:01, Manager attempts to download the Branch Profit Report using their previously valid Access Token.

TC ID & Scenario: TC41 (Logic - Orphaned Branch): Terminate the ONLY Manager of Branch X.
